text:
B: Hi, can you hear me? I'm Gemma, in Hornchurch.
A: Yeah. Shazia. Walsall.
B: Hi. So what do you do, Shazia?
A: At home. Three kids. Used to work in a warehouse.
B: Right. How old are they?
A: Seventeen, fourteen, nine.
B: Okay, so you're in the thick of it. Mine are eleven and eight. Ruby's just started secondary and the homework is ridiculous, honestly, it's every night.
A: Wait till they're seventeen. My eldest is doing A-levels. She's up till midnight.
B: What's she doing?
A: Biology, chemistry, psychology. She wants to do something in healthcare at uni.
B: Oh, I did biology and psychology. I'm a speech and language therapist. Has she looked at that?
A: Don't know. What do you actually do, then?
B: Kids with speech and language delays, mostly. Working out where they're stuck, then giving the parents things to practise at home. I did ten years in the NHS before I went private. And honestly, I was the first in my family to go to uni. My dad worked at Ford. So if she wants it, she can do it.
A: My dad worked in a foundry. Nobody went. She'd be the first.
B: Well, there you go. You must be proud.
A: I am. I just don't want her going far, to be honest. She's on about Manchester.
B: Manchester's a good place for that, though. And it's what, an hour and a half on the train?
A: It's still far. You're in London. Yours'd be on the tube.
B: That's fair. I'd probably be the same, actually, if I'm being honest. Ruby leaving would wreck me.
A: Yeah. That's it.
B: What about the fourteen-year-old?
A: Zain. PlayStation. All night if I let him.
B: We have screen time rows constantly. I've got a timer on the router now. I think you just have to be really strict with it, set the limit and stick to it, otherwise they walk all over you.
A: No, I don't really agree with that. You can set all the timers you want. He's fourteen, he'll just go on his phone instead. You've got to pick what you're fighting about.
B: Hm. Okay, yeah, maybe. Alfie's only eight, so I've still got the upper hand.
A: For now.
B: Ha. For now. Erm, did you get on with the puzzle at the start?
A: Not really. Did you?
B: Finished it. Just.
A: Course you did.
B: Sorry, that's the second person who's said that to me today.
A: It's the kitchen. It looks like you've got everything sorted.
B: Honestly, the school letters on that worktop are about three weeks old.
